bullets.title: ORCL: F1Q27 triple-digit IaaS growth; $30B AI bookings; raises FY27 guidance
bullets.body: Oracle posted F1Q27 revenue of $19.35B (+30% y/y, +1.1% beat), OCI growing 121% y/y to $7.4B, with $30B+ in new AI cloud contracts boosting RPO to $664B (+46% y/y). The company delivered 850MW of capacity and 300K+ GPUs in the quarter (3x Q4), completed the $20B ATM equity raise, and raised FY27 EPS guidance to $8.10 vs prior $8.05 and confirmed 'at least $90B' revenue. Older-gen GPU renewals are pricing at ~20% premium, validating compute scarcity. Buy-side broadly bullish; GS, JPM, Citi all maintain bullish ratings with PTs of $300-330+.

bullets.title: ADBE Q3: ARR collapses 39% y/y; Hedgeye maintains top short; monetization thesis challenged
bullets.body: Adobe beat Q3 revenue ($6.76B) and EPS ($6.13) slightly, but net new ARR plunged 39% y/y to $400M—well below the historical norm—and RPO growth decelerated to 8% y/y (first sub-10% since FY22). Q4 guide requires a 1.94x Q3-to-Q4 step-up in ARR vs. historical 1.39-1.41x, making the reaffirmed +10.2% FY ARR guide look aggressive. Street is split: JPM maintains OW ($315 PT dec-27), Citi cuts to $250 (Neutral), Hedgeye remains top short. Key bear thesis: management prioritizing freemium MAU acquisition while organic revenue growth crosses into high-single digits.

bullets.title: RH Q2 margin blowout; 4Q guide requires unproven Estates ramp—stock up ~7% post-earnings
bullets.body: RH posted Q2 gross margin of 48.2% vs consensus 43.3% and adj. EBITDA margin of 19.4% vs Street 12.8%, partly benefiting from ~$55M in tariff refunds. Q3 guide calls for +5-6% revenue growth with Estates contributing ~2pts; Q4 guide of +16-21% requires ~8pts from Estates. Morgan Stanley maintains OW at $210 with a $50 wide bull/bear case. UBS stays Neutral, arguing the tariff refund masked the underlying margin story and that 4Q relies on an untested product category.

bullets.title: META: JPM upgrades to OW $820 PT on Muse AI agent launch; 10x usage vs. test cohorts
bullets.body: JPM upgraded META to Overweight from Neutral, raising PT to $820 (23x 2028E GAAP EPS of $35.44). Muse personal AI agent reached #2-4 on US App Store within days, with early usage running 10x above testing cohorts per Meta's Chief AI Officer. The Watermelon model (trained with 10x more compute than Muse Spark 1.3) is expected in October, and a 1GW Prometheus compute cluster in Ohio is already training post-Watermelon models. Wells Fargo also upgraded META to OW ($640→$820 PT) on frontier AI optionality beyond advertising.

bullets.title: SHOP: Bernstein initiates OW $160 PT; Mizuho & JPM dismiss Meta Muse disintermediation fears
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated Shopify at Outperform with a $160 PT (26% upside), catalyzing a ~3.5% move on the day. Separately, Mizuho and JPM both issued notes arguing that Meta Muse routes through Stripe Link but does NOT bypass Shopify Payments—virtual card transactions process normally with no economic change to Shopify, and a native Shop Pay integration is coming soon. JPM reiterates OW at $185 PT; new AI buyer orders from agent sources converting at ~2x traditional channel rates.

bullets.title: AMD: Data center revenue to 2x in 2027; MI450 ramping Q3; CPU TAM now $220B by 2030
bullets.body: At the Citi TMT and GS Communacopia conferences, AMD management reiterated datacenter revenue will more than double in 2027 on the MI450/Helios ramp (starting Q3, step-up in Q4 and Q1:27). Server CPU supply growing 80% in H2:26 and 70% in 2027; Venice CPUs broadly supported at launch. AMD revised its agentic CPU TAM to $220B by 2030 (vs. $25B in 2025) and is targeting ~50% server dollar share. Citi maintains Buy at $575 PT.

bullets.title: NVDA: DOJ investigating Groq licensing deal; CEO reaffirms +70% FY27 revenue growth
bullets.body: Reports emerged that the DOJ is investigating Nvidia's ~$17B licensing arrangement with Groq, allegedly structured to avoid antitrust review. Despite this headwind, NVDA fell ~5% w/w. The CEO reiterated 70% revenue growth for FY27 citing reach across AI labs and cloud providers. NVDA's $500B+ capital partnership framework remains intact, with older-gen GPU renewals pricing at 20% premiums. MS maintains OW at $300 PT (+30% upside).

bullets.title: MSFT: Plans to 3x datacenter capacity to 38GW by 2032; E7 attach 'incredibly strong start'
bullets.body: Microsoft disclosed plans to expand total compute capacity from ~12GW today to ~38GW by 2032 (~4-4.5GW added annually), with AI-specific GPU capacity growing from ~2GW to roughly one-third of the total. At the Citi TMT conference, management highlighted usage-based billing (UBB) launched June 1 as a significant monetization driver, and E7 SKU attachments are off to an 'incredibly strong start.' OpenAI suspended new ChatGPT Pro subscriptions due to unprecedented Astra demand, reinforcing tight compute supply.

bullets.title: TSM August revenue +53% y/y; NVDA to consume 55-60% of N3 wafers in 2027
bullets.body: TSMC reported August revenue of NT$514.8B, up 53% y/y, tracking at the mid-to-high end of Q3 guidance. JPM and UBS both note that NVDA's Rubin/Vera ramp will consume 55-60% of all N3 wafers in 2027 (vs <10% in H1:26), while CPU ramps from Google, Amazon, and Microsoft further strain N3 supply. The shortage is unlikely to ease materially in 2027 even with Fab 18 P9 and Fab 21 P2 Arizona additions.

bullets.title: AVGO: Reaffirms AI revenue doubling to $115B (FY27) and $230B (FY28); supply constrained
bullets.body: At the GS Communacopia conference, Broadcom reaffirmed its framework: AI infrastructure revenue ~doubles each of the next two fiscal years, reaching ~$115B in FY27 and ~$230B in FY28. The company also announced a $35B XPV partnership to fund 20GW+ of compute capacity. Custom ASICs (XPUs) are forecast to grow from 34% to 66% of incremental AI compute capacity by 2028, structurally benefiting AVGO across Google, OpenAI, Meta, and Meta MTIA programs.

bullets.title: GLW: Verizon multi-billion fiber deal; $20B run-rate accelerated to Q3; China Renaissance initiates Buy at $238
bullets.body: Corning and Verizon announced a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar supply agreement for 80M+ miles of high-density optical fiber through 2032, supporting broadband expansion and AI hyperscaler DCI. Corning said this pulls forward the $20B sales run-rate target one quarter to Q3 (vs. prior guidance), with 4Q expected to exceed 3Q and high-teens y/y growth into 2027. Citi Buy at $220, China Renaissance initiated at Buy with a $238 PT (54% upside).

bullets.title: NBIS: Citi Buy $324 PT; Palantir partnership; compute pricing at $20-25M/MW near-term
bullets.body: At the Citi TMT conference, Nebius management highlighted AI infrastructure demand extending into 2028, with spot pricing at $40-50M/MW and longer-term contracts pricing at $20-25M/MW. The Palantir partnership positions Nebius as preferred sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise clients. Truist initiates Buy at $355 PT (+48% upside). Key risk: customer concentration (MSFT + META ~40% of FY26 ARR).

bullets.title: CRWV: Compute pricing underappreciated; $1M/MW improvement worth $17/share
bullets.body: Multiple sources highlight that consensus is underpricing CoreWeave's compute realization. 22V estimates actual $/MW/year realizations at $15-20M (vs. ~$12M in consensus) on 5.5GW of its ~8GW open portfolio, with each $1M/MW uplift worth ~$17/share. IREN has validated rising pricing at $25M/MW for 3-year deals and $40M/MW for sub-1-year spot deals. Oracle renewing older-gen GPU contracts at 20% premiums corroborates the scarcity premium dynamic.

bullets.title: PLTR: DA Davidson raises PT to $250 on AI sovereignty and NVDA supply chain work
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded Palantir to Buy and raised PT from $200 to $250, citing institutional investor re-engagement after AIPCon11 focused on AI sovereignty themes. The firm highlighted PLTR's supply management system built for NVIDIA's Nemotron that addresses critical supply chain challenges. Separately, UBS hosted an update call flagging positive learnings from a CFO dinner.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: DOJ issues Second Request on merger; deal still expected to close H1 2027
bullets.body: Fox Corp and Roku each received a DOJ 'Second Request' for additional information on the $22B merger (Fox paying $96 cash + stock per ROKU share at $160/share). The deal closure timeline is extended but Fox still expects H1 2027 close. FOXA management at GS Communacopia reiterated record FY27 outlook, Tubi 35%+ revenue growth, and ~$400M in run-rate synergies. DOJ concern centers on potential content favoritism (Tubi vs. Roku Channel) and competitive overlap.

bullets.title: ANET: Raises 2026 revenue guide to $12.6B; scale-up pilots expected 2027, commercial revenue 2028
bullets.body: At the Citi TMT conference, Arista raised its 2026 revenue guidance to ~$12.6B (40% growth), with purchase commitments tripling to $9.6B y/y. Supply conditions have improved with arrangements locked through 2027. Scale-across networking (~1/3 of AI sales) is expanding; scale-up revenue remains excluded from guidance with pilots beginning in 2027 and commercial revenue expected in 2028. Citi Buy at $215 PT.

bullets.title: CSCO: $100B+ networking upgrade opportunity; $7.5B FY27 AI revenue target; Silicon One to be majority by FY29
bullets.body: At GS Communacopia, Cisco outlined a $100B+ addressable networking upgrade opportunity from end-of-life Catalyst 4K/6K switches. Management targets $7.5B in AI revenue for FY27, built on $9B+ in AI orders in FY26 (60% Silicon One systems, 40% Acacia optics). Silicon One is <10% of switches shipped today but is expected to be a majority by FY29. Citi Buy at $139 PT (+29% upside).

bullets.title: HIMS: JPM initiates Neutral $32 PT; Novo Wegovy partnership with 125K+ shipments in 6 weeks
bullets.body: JPM's Bryan Smilek initiated coverage of Hims & Hers at Neutral with a December 2027 PT of $32, noting the pivot from compounded to branded FDA-approved GLP-1s. The Novo Wegovy partnership has shipped 125K+ prescriptions in 6 weeks, and management projects 2026 GLP-1 revenue of $1.1B (+46% y/y) and targets $6.5B+ revenue and $1.3B+ EBITDA by 2030. Near-term risk: branded GLP-1 gross margins are lower than compounded, pressuring 2026 adj. EBITDA margins to ~9.2%.

bullets.title: DKNG: Early NFL season is key—Predictions unit EBITDA timing (2027 vs 2028) hinges on customer acquisition pace
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on DraftKings; management frames the business as a ~$1B EBITDA core OSB/iGaming operation with Predictions as a large call option currently assigned negative value. The timing of Predictions EBITDA inflection depends on early NFL customer acquisition pace—aggressive acquisition creates near-term profit pressure but could pull EBITDA harvest into 2027, while gradual acquisition mirrors prior state OSB rollouts and pushes to 2028. DraftKings' NFL, CFB, and MLB markets are now running on its proprietary DKX exchange.
